requirements.subject: ent:attribute
requirements.canonical: An attribute IS a means to give a special characterization or meaning, such as a specific presentation format, a specific encoding, an encoding variant or a user-defined property, to a TTCN-3 language element.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 uses attributes to give special characterization/meaning to language elements such as specific presentation format, specific encoding and encoding variants, and user-defined properties.

requirements.subject: ent:attribute
requirements.canonical: An attribute MAY be associated with a TTCN-3 language element by means of the `with` statement.
requirements.original: Attributes can be associated with TTCN-3 language elements by means of the with statement.

requirements.subject: ent:with-statement
requirements.canonical: A `with` statement MAY be applied to a module, to a global module definition, and to a local definition in the module control function, in a test case, in a function, in an altstep, in a statement block or in a component type definition.
requirements.original: The with statement can be applied to modules, global module definitions and to local definitions in control, test cases, functions, altsteps, statement blocks and in component type definitions.

ambiguity.issue: 'control' is used for the module control function; the outdated term 'control part' is implied.

requirements.subject: ent:with-statement
requirements.canonical: A `with` statement MAY associate attributes to a single language element.
requirements.original: A with statement may associate attributes to a single language element

requirements.subject: ent:with-statement
requirements.canonical: A `with` statement MAY associate attributes, recursively, to fields or elements of a structured type, in the same way as specified in clauses 6.2.1.1 and 6.2.3.2.
requirements.original: or to elements or fields of structured types (in a recursive way) ... the same way as specified in clauses 6.2.1.1 and 6.2.3.2.

requirements.subject: ent:with-statement
requirements.canonical: A `with` statement MAY associate attributes to members of a component type or a port type, in the same way as specified in clauses 6.2.1.1 and 6.2.3.2.
requirements.original: or to members of component or port types, the same way as specified in clauses 6.2.1.1 and 6.2.3.2.

requirements.subject: ent:with-statement
requirements.canonical: A `with` statement associated with a single structured type definition MAY associate attributes to several fields of that type by listing the fields in the attribute statement.
requirements.original: It is also possible to associate attributes to a number of language elements by, e.g. listing fields of a structured type in an attribute statement associated with a single type definition

requirements.subject: ent:with-statement
requirements.canonical: A `with` statement associated with a surrounding scope unit or a group MAY associate attributes to all language elements of that scope unit or group.
requirements.original: or associating a with statement to the surrounding scope unit or group of language elements.

requirements.subject: ent:with-statement
requirements.canonical: A `with` statement MAY follow any module, any global definition inside module and group declarations, and any local definition in component types and in statement blocks inside behaviour definitions.
requirements.original: A with statement can follow any module, any global definition inside module and group declarations as well as any local definition in component types and statement blocks inside behaviour definitions.

requirements.subject: ent:synonym-type
requirements.canonical: An attribute MAY be attached to a synonym type.
requirements.original: Attributes can be attached to synonym types (clause 6.4).

requirements.subject: ent:with-statement
requirements.condition: the synonym type is a structured type
requirements.canonical: If a synonym type is a structured type, the attributes in the `with` statement of the synonym type MAY reference fields or elements of that structured type.
requirements.original: If the synonym type is a structured type, attributes in the with statement may reference fields or elements of this structured type.

requirements.subject: ent:attribute
requirements.canonical: An attribute definition that is directly attached to a lower scope unit IS overriding a general attribute definition of a higher scope.
requirements.original: An attribute definition that is directly attached to a lower scope unit will override a general attribute definition in a higher scope

requirements.subject: ent:attribute
requirements.canonical: An attribute definition that is directly attached to a lower scope unit IS overriding a type-specific attribute inherited from a type reference.
requirements.original: An attribute definition that is directly attached to a lower scope unit will override ... a type-specific attribute inherited from a type reference.

requirements.subject: ent:attribute
requirements.canonical: An attribute inherited from a type reference IS overriding a general attribute of a higher scope unit that contains the type reference.
requirements.original: Attributes inherited from a type reference will override general attributes from a higher scope unit containing the type reference.

requirements.subject: ent:with-statement
requirements.canonical: A `with` statement that is placed inside the scope of another `with` statement SHALL override the outer `with` statement.
requirements.original: A with statement that is placed inside the scope of another with statement shall override the outermost with.

ambiguity.issue: 'the outermost with' can be read literally (only the outermost of several nested with statements) or as 'any enclosing with'. The second reading is chosen because the nested overriding scheme of example 2 implies it.
readings: A `with` statement that is placed inside the scope of another `with` statement SHALL override every enclosing `with` statement.
A `with` statement that is placed inside the scope of another `with` statement SHALL override only the outermost `with` statement.

requirements.subject: ent:with-statement
requirements.canonical: A `with` statement associated with a group nested inside another group SHALL override the `with` statement of the enclosing group.
requirements.original: This shall also apply to the use of the with statement with groups.

requirements.subject: ent:attribute
requirements.condition: multiple attributes of the same kind are allowed
requirements.canonical: If multiple attributes of the same kind are allowed, an overriding attribute definition IS overriding all of the attributes of that kind, unless specified otherwise.
requirements.original: If multiple attributes of the same type are allowed, all of them are overridden unless specified otherwise.

ambiguity.issue: 'unless specified otherwise' does not say where the exception is specified (e.g. clause 27.1.2.2 for multiple encodings); 'type' is used for the kind of attribute. Reading 1 is chosen.
readings: If multiple attributes of the same kind are allowed, an overriding attribute definition IS overriding all of them, except where another clause of the standard specifies a different rule.
If multiple attributes of the same kind are allowed, an overriding attribute definition IS overriding all of them, unless the overriding attribute definition itself specifies otherwise.

requirements.subject: ent:attribute
requirements.canonical: An attribute defined for a synonym type IS NOT overriding an existing attribute of a field or element of the synonym type.
requirements.original: Attributes defined for a synonym type do not override existing attributes of fields or elements of this synonym type.

requirements.subject: ent:attribute
requirements.condition: the field or element has no valid attribute
requirements.canonical: An attribute of a synonym type IS applied to a field or element of the synonym type only if the field or element has no valid attribute.
requirements.original: The attributes are applied to the fields or elements of synonym types only if the fields or elements have no valid attributes.

requirements.subject: ent:local-modifier
requirements.canonical: An attribute with the `@local` modifier IS overriding attributes from a higher scope.
requirements.original: Attributes with the @local modifier override attributes from higher scope

requirements.subject: ent:local-modifier
requirements.canonical: An attribute with the `@local` modifier IS valid for the associated language element only.
requirements.original: but they are valid for the associated language element only.

requirements.subject: ent:local-modifier
requirements.canonical: An attribute with the `@local` modifier IS NOT affecting definitions inside the associated language element, because it is transparent to lower scopes.
requirements.original: They do not affect definitions inside the associated language element as the @local attribute is completely transparent to lower scopes.

requirements.subject: ent:attribute
requirements.canonical: An attribute from a higher scope IS affecting the language elements of lower scopes even if an attribute with the `@local` modifier is attached to a scope between them.
requirements.original: Attributes from higher scope will still affect attributes in lower scopes even if the @local attribute is between them.

ambiguity.issue: 'affect attributes in lower scopes' is read as affecting the language elements of lower scopes (they inherit the higher-scope attribute), not as modifying explicit lower-scope attributes.
readings: An attribute from a higher scope IS applied to the language elements of lower scopes even if an attribute with the `@local` modifier is attached to an intermediate scope.
An attribute from a higher scope IS overriding explicitly declared attributes in lower scopes even if an attribute with the `@local` modifier is attached to an intermediate scope.

requirements.subject: ent:local-modifier
requirements.canonical: An attribute with the `@local` modifier associated with a module or a group IS valid.
requirements.original: NOTE: Attributes with the @local modifier associated to modules and groups are valid

requirements.subject: ent:local-modifier
requirements.canonical: An attribute with the `@local` modifier associated with a module or a group IS NOT affecting the definitions inside the module or group.
requirements.original: but do not affect the definitions inside them.

requirements.subject: ent:override-directive
requirements.canonical: An attribute definition in a lower scope, or an attribute inherited from a referenced type, MAY be overwritten from a higher scope by using the `override` directive.
requirements.original: An attribute definition in a lower scope or those inherited from a referenced type can be overwritten in a higher scope by using the override directive.

requirements.subject: ent:override-directive
requirements.canonical: The `override` directive IS overriding the specified attribute for all declarations at all lower scopes that do not also declare the specified attribute.
requirements.original: The override directive overrides the specified attribute for all declarations at all lower scopes that do not also declare the specified attribute.

ambiguity.issue: The sentence seems to conflict with 27.1.2.0-s022, which states that the override directive overwrites attribute definitions of lower scopes. Example 6 (MyRecordD.fieldC keeps RuleC against the group's override RuleA) suggests that a lower declaration with its own override directive is kept. Reading 1 is chosen.
readings: The `override` directive IS overriding the specified attribute for all lower-scope declarations, except those lower-scope declarations that declare the same attribute with an `override` directive themselves.
The `override` directive IS overriding the specified attribute only for lower-scope declarations that do not declare the specified attribute at all.

requirements.subject: ent:override-directive
requirements.condition: the override directive is applied to a type reference
requirements.canonical: If the `override` directive is applied to a type reference, the `override` directive IS NOT affecting the attributes of the original referenced type.
requirements.original: If the override directive is applied to a type reference, it does not affect the attributes of the original referenced type.

requirements.subject: ent:attribute
requirements.canonical: An attribute definition directly attached to a field or element of a structured type IS overriding the corresponding attribute of the structured type for the identified field or element.
requirements.original: An attribute definition directly attached to a field or element of a structured type overrides the corresponding attribute of the structured type, as regards the identified field or element.

requirements.subject: ent:override-directive
requirements.canonical: An attribute with the `override` directive applied to a synonym type IS overriding the attributes of all fields or elements of the synonym type, unless the synonym type definition contains an explicit attribute definition for the field or element.
requirements.original: Override attribute applied to a synonym type (clause 6.4) overrides attributes of all fields or elements of the synonym type unless the synonym type definition contains an explicit attribute definition for the field or element.

ambiguity.issue: 'Override attribute' is used for an attribute carrying the override directive.

non_requirement.reason: pointer to clause 27.1.2.1 (variant overwriting rules, extracted from 27.1.2.1-s001..s008)
